# AGENTS.md — this OpenSpace site

This repository is an OpenSpace website. The content and design choices live here; the code
lives in versioned npm packages (`@omniharmonic/openspace-site-kit`). Publishing happens automatically when
changes land on `main` (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`).

## Rules

1. **Content lives in `content/`.** Never hand-edit `src/`, `astro.config.mjs` or the
   workflow unless you were asked for a custom block (`src/overrides/`).
2. **Preserve ids.** Every page (`pg_`), section (`sec_`), block (`blk_`), media item (`med_`)
   and form (`frm_`) has a stable id. Keep ids when editing; new ids are the prefix plus 10
   lowercase Crockford base32 characters (no i, l, o, u).
3. **Only valid block types and fields** (listed below; full JSON Schema at
   https://schema.openspace.host/v1/). Unknown fields fail the build.
4. **Styles change through tokens** in `content/styles.json` (palette, type pairing, density,
   shape…), never inline CSS. Sections pick one of five color themes.
5. **Never put secrets in content** (API keys, tokens, passwords). `openspace check` fails on them.
   Members-only and password pages are only stubs here (a page file with `contentRef` and no
   sections): their content is kept by the OpenSpace Hub and never committed. Edit them in
   Studio or with the Hub's MCP tools; never add sections to a stub (they would be public).
6. **Run `npx openspace check` before committing.** It validates schemas, links, image references,
   size budgets and scans for secrets.
7. Write real copy in the owner's voice. No placeholder text, no invented testimonials, prices
   or facts — ask the owner.

## Layout

```
openspace.json               site id, Hub URL, deploy target, features (https://schema.openspace.host/v1/site-config.json)
content/site.json            title, navigation, header, footer, SEO defaults, redirects
content/styles.json          design tokens and Site Styles choices
content/media.json           metadata for files in media/ (alt text, size, focal point, credit)
content/pages/home.json      the home page (slug ""); other pages mirror their URL:
content/pages/about.json     → /about/      content/pages/services/pricing.json → /services/pricing/
content/collections/<name>/_collection.json   collection kind, list + item page layout, feeds
content/collections/<name>/<slug>.mdoc        one item: YAML frontmatter + Markdoc body
content/components/<name>.json                a custom component (designer section)
media/                       images ≤ 2400px on the long edge, audio, files
```

A page is `{ id, title, slug, seo?, sections: [...] }`; a section has a `layout` (`stack` with
column spans that add up to 12, or `grid`) and `blocks`; a block is
`{ id, type, v, fields, variant?, style? }`.

## Custom components

Designer sections for moments the blocks can't express. `content/components/<name>.json` holds
typed `fields`, sample `defaults`, a logic-light `template` (`{{field}}`, `{{rich f}}`,
`{{image f}}`, `{{button f label=g}}`, `{{#if}}`, `{{#each}}`; no scripts, no raw HTML), scoped
`css` on theme tokens (`var(--os-color-…)`, `var(--os-space-…)`) and optional `js` (the body of
`function (root, ctx)`, progressive enhancement only, no network). Pages use one as a block
`{ "type": "component/<name>", "v": <version>, "fields": {…} }`. Every word, image and link is a
field, so owners keep editing in Studio. Prefer blocks and presets; `openspace check` enforces
the component gates (accessibility, reduced motion, budgets).

## Collection items (Markdoc)

Frontmatter follows the collection kind (blog, events, portfolio, podcast, products): `title`,
`status` (draft | scheduled | published), `publishAt` for scheduled items, `excerpt`, `image`,
`categories`, `tags`, plus kind-specific fields (`date`, `start`/`end`, `price` in minor units…).

The body is Markdown prose plus Markdoc tags. **Tags map 1:1 to blocks**: the tag name is the
block type, attributes are its fields, and content between the tags fills its text:

```markdoc
{% gallery layout="grid" images=["media/2026/10/a.jpg", "media/2026/10/b.jpg"] /%}

{% button href="/schedule" variant="primary" %}See the schedule{% /button %}
```

No scripts or raw HTML: anything interactive is a block.

## Running locally

- `npm install`, then `npm run dev` for a live preview.
- `npx openspace mcp` starts the local MCP server so an AI assistant can edit through the same
  structured operations as the Studio.
- `npm run build` builds the site into `dist/` exactly as the publish workflow does.

## Blocks

### `accordion` — Accordion / FAQ

Expandable questions and answers, with schema.org FAQPage markup. Use: FAQs, policies, class or service details — anything visitors scan for one answer. 4–10 items works best. Avoid: Hiding essential information (prices, hours) only inside an accordion; answers longer than a short paragraph or list.

- Variants: `lines`, `cards`, `minimal`
- Fields: `items: list of { question: text ≤ 160, answer: richText }`, `exclusive: boolean`, `openFirst: boolean`, `faqSchema: boolean`

### `audio` — Audio / podcast episode

Plays one audio file — a podcast episode, track, talk or guided practice — with its notes. Use: Episode pages, music and talks. Add listen links for the podcast apps the show is on. `minimal` is just the player and title. Avoid: Autoplay (never supported); audio without a written summary or transcript link for deaf visitors.

- Variants: `episode`, `card`, `minimal`
- Fields: `audio?: media`, `title: text ≤ 120`, `show?: text ≤ 80`, `episode?: number`, `date?: text ≤ 10`, `description?: text ≤ 600`, `cover?: image { src, alt }`, `links: list of { platform: "apple" | "spotify" | "youtube" | "rss" | "other", label?: text ≤ 40, link: link }`, `credit?: text ≤ 200`

### `before-after` — Before / after

Compares two matching images with a draggable divider: renovations, retouching, seasons. Use: When the difference between two shots of the same view is the point. Use images with identical framing and size. Avoid: Unrelated images; misleading edits; more than one or two per page.

- Variants: `labels`, `minimal`
- Fields: `before: image { src, alt }`, `after: image { src, alt }`, `beforeLabel: text ≤ 30`, `afterLabel: text ≤ 30`, `start: number`, `aspect: "original" | "1:1" | "4:5" | "2:3" | "3:2" | "16:9" | "21:9"`, `caption?: text ≤ 200`

### `booking` — Booking

Lets visitors book an appointment through the owner's Cal.com or Calendly page. Use: Services, coaching, consultations and classes booked by time slot. The scheduler loads only after a click, so the page stays fast and private. `button` just links out. Avoid: Scheduling links the owner hasn't set up; more than one booking block per page.

- Variants: `inline`, `split`, `button`
- Fields: `url: text ≤ 300`, `provider: "auto" | "cal" | "calendly"`, `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `description?: text ≤ 300`, `buttonLabel: text ≤ 30`, `height: "640" | "760" | "900"`

### `button` — Button

A clear call to action linking to a page, booking tool, email or file. Use: Once per screenful for the main action. Add a second (secondary-style) action only when it's a genuine alternative. Avoid: Several primary buttons side by side; vague labels like 'Click here' or 'Learn more' without context.

- Variants: `default`, `large`, `full-width`
- Fields: `label: text ≤ 40`, `link: link`, `role: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary"`, `secondaryLabel?: text ≤ 40`, `secondaryLink?: link`, `note?: text ≤ 120`

### `card` — Card

One self-contained item — a service, offer, event or article teaser — with an optional link. Use: Place 2–4 cards side by side in stack columns for services or offers. `overlay` sets text on the photo; `horizontal` suits wide columns. Avoid: Long body text (keep under ~40 words); different aspect ratios across cards in a row.

- Variants: `stacked`, `horizontal`, `overlay`, `minimal`

### `chart` — Chart

Shows a small set of numbers as a bar, column, line or pie chart. Use: Up to ~12 values that tell one story: results, survey answers, growth over time. `line` for change over time, `pie` for shares of a whole (2–6 slices). Avoid: Invented or unsourced figures; pies with many slices; charts that need more than one series.

- Variants: `bar`, `column`, `line`, `pie`
- Fields: `title: text ≤ 120`, `description?: text ≤ 240`, `rows: list of { label: text ≤ 40, value: number }`, `prefix?: text ≤ 4`, `suffix?: text ≤ 12`, `showValues: boolean`, `showTable: boolean`

### `columns` — Columns

Parallel content in columns: a feature trio, numbered steps, or short offers. Use: When 2–4 items share the same shape. `steps` numbers them for a process; `cards` puts each on a surface. Avoid: Uneven text lengths across columns; more than four columns; long paragraphs.

- Variants: `plain`, `cards`, `steps`
- Fields: `items: list of { image?: image { src, alt }, heading: text ≤ 80, body: richText, link?: link, linkLabel?: text ≤ 30 }`, `columns: "2" | "3" | "4" | "5" | "6"`, `aspect: "original" | "1:1" | "4:5" | "2:3" | "3:2" | "16:9" | "21:9"`

### `contact-info` — Contact details

How to reach or visit the business: address, phone, email. Use: Contact pages, footers and beside a map or form. `columns` lays the details side by side on wide screens. Avoid: Personal phone numbers or addresses the owner hasn't chosen to publish.

- Variants: `card`, `list`, `columns`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 60`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `name?: text ≤ 80`, `address?: text ≤ 240`, `phone?: text ≤ 30`, `email?: text ≤ 120`, `directions: boolean`, `note?: text ≤ 200`

### `countdown` — Countdown

A live countdown to a moment: a launch, a sale ending, an event starting. Use: Time-bound announcements near a call to action. The exact date is always printed too, so it still works without JavaScript. Avoid: Fake urgency (timers that reset); countdowns to dates that have long passed.

- Variants: `boxes`, `inline`, `large`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `target: text ≤ 32`, `showSeconds: boolean`, `doneMessage: text ≤ 160`, `buttonLabel?: text ≤ 30`, `link?: link`

### `divider` — Divider with ornament

A decorative separator: a small ornament or label between thin lines. Use: Between passages of long-form text, menus or story pages where a plain line feels too stark. One or two per page. Avoid: Separating every block; ornaments that clash with a minimal site style.

- Variants: `lines`, `ornament`, `label`
- Fields: `ornament: "flourish" | "star" | "diamond" | "dots" | "leaf" | "wave" | "asterism"`, `label?: text ≤ 40`, `length: "short" | "half" | "full"`, `color: color`

### `donation` — Donation

Collects donations: preset or custom amounts, one-time or monthly. Use: Non-profits, community projects and creators. Say concretely what a gift pays for. `link` mode points to an existing donation page (Open Collective, Stripe Payment Link…). Avoid: Amounts or causes the owner hasn't approved; promising tax deductibility without confirming it.

- Variants: `card`, `inline`, `split`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `description?: text ≤ 400`, `mode: "checkout" | "link"`, `currency: "USD" | "EUR" | "GBP" | "CAD" | "AUD" | "NZD" | "CHF" | "SEK" | "NOK" | "DKK" | "JPY"`, `amounts: list of { amount: number }`, `allowCustom: boolean`, `frequency: "both" | "once" | "monthly"`, `buttonLabel: text ≤ 30`, `link?: link`, `note?: text ≤ 200`

### `embed` — Embed / Code

Embeds third-party widgets (booking, surveys, tickets, playlists) by URL or HTML snippet. Use: Only when no dedicated block exists for the service. Avoid: Tracking scripts; snippets with secrets or API keys; embedding YouTube/Vimeo (use the video block) or maps (use the map block).

- Variants: `plain`, `framed`
- Fields: `embed: embed`, `title: text ≤ 120`, `aspect: "auto" | "16:9" | "4:3" | "1:1"`, `height: number`

### `events` — Events

Shows events from the events collection: dates, times, places and a way to register. Use: Home, schedule and community pages. `calendar` shows month grids with an agenda below; `list` is the most scannable. Avoid: Typing events into text blocks (add them to the events collection so they stay in sync).

- Variants: `list`, `cards`, `calendar`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `source: reference`, `showImage: boolean`, `showLocation: boolean`, `showExcerpt: boolean`, `registerLabel: text ≤ 30`, `emptyMessage: text ≤ 160`, `structuredData: boolean`

### `form` — Form

Collects enquiries, bookings requests, RSVPs or applications into the owner's Inbox. Use: Contact pages and anywhere visitors need to send structured details. Pair with a short text block explaining what happens next. Avoid: Long forms (keep under ~8 fields); asking for sensitive data; password or payment fields (not allowed — payments go through checkout).

- Variants: `default`, `card`, `underline`
- Fields: `form: form`

### `gallery` — Gallery

Several related photographs shown together. Use: Portfolios, spaces, events and products. `grid` for tidy sets, `masonry` and `strips` for mixed orientations, `carousel` for many images in little space, `slideshow` for one large image at a time. Avoid: Mixing unrelated photos; fewer than three images (use the image block); captions that repeat alt text.

- Variants: `grid`, `carousel`, `masonry`, `slideshow`, `strips`
- Fields: `images: list of { image: image { src, alt }, caption?: text ≤ 160, link?: link }`, `aspect: "auto" | "original" | "1:1" | "4:5" | "2:3" | "3:2" | "16:9" | "21:9"`, `columns: "2" | "3" | "4" | "5"`, `fit?: "cover" | "contain"`, `lightbox: boolean`, `showCaptions: boolean`

### `heading` — Heading

A section heading with optional eyebrow and supporting line. Use: To open a section or introduce a group of blocks. `rule` adds a short accent line above, `eyebrow-rule` a short accent line between the eyebrow and the heading, `underline` a line below, `split` puts the subheading beside the heading on wide screens. Avoid: Using headings for emphasis inside body copy (use text); skipping levels (h2 → h4); more than one Heading 1 per page.

- Variants: `plain`, `rule`, `underline`, `split`, `eyebrow-rule`
- Fields: `eyebrow?: text ≤ 60`, `text: text ≤ 160`, `level: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `size: "auto" | "display" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `phoneSize?: "auto" | "display" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `subheading?: text ≤ 280`

### `hours` — Opening hours

When a place is open, day by day. Use: Contact, visit and footer areas of shops, studios, cafés and offices. Pair with the contact card or map. Avoid: Hours the owner hasn't confirmed; using it for event times (use events).

- Variants: `table`, `compact`, `card`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 60`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `rows: list of { day: "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat" | "sun", opens?: text ≤ 5, closes?: text ≤ 5, closed: boolean }`, `note?: text ≤ 200`

### `icon-list` — Icon list

A scannable list of features, amenities, benefits or what's included. Use: Services and pricing pages, 'what to expect' sections. 3–8 items. Avoid: Using icons that don't match the meaning; paragraphs instead of one-line points.

A single photograph or illustration. Use: To show the place, the people, the work or the product. Keep aspect ratios consistent within a section. `caption-overlay` suits atmospheric shots; `inset` frames an image on a soft surface. ### `line` — Line

A visual divider between pieces of content. Use: To separate groups inside a section, or as a short accent rule above a heading (`length: short`, color `accent`). Avoid: Lines between every block; using lines where whitespace or a section change would do.

A link-in-bio list: a few large, tappable links under a photo and one-line bio. Use: On a dedicated links page shared from social profiles, or a compact 'start here' list. ### `map` — Map

Shows where a place is, with the address and a link to full maps. Use: Contact and visit pages for any business with a physical location. ### `marquee` — Scrolling text

A continuously scrolling line of short phrases, like a ticker or a shop-window band. Use: For energy between sections: offerings, places, a short slogan. 3–8 phrases of 1–3 words. `band` sets it on an accent strip. Avoid: Essential information (it moves and can be paused); long sentences; more than one per page. It never moves for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

### `member-login` — Member sign-in

Lets members sign in with an emailed link, or tells visitors that content is members-only. Use: On the members' sign-in page (`form`), at the top of a members-only page's public teaser (`gated`), or as a slim prompt (`banner`). Members need the Cloudflare hosting option. Avoid: Putting the members-only content itself on a public page; asking for passwords.

### `newsletter` — Newsletter signup

Collects email subscribers (double opt-in) for the owner's newsletter. Use: Footers, the end of blog posts, and dedicated 'stay in touch' sections. Say what subscribers get and how often. Avoid: Promising content or frequency the owner hasn't agreed to; more than one signup per page.

### `pricing` — Pricing table

Compares plans, packages or tiers with prices and what each includes. Use: Pricing, membership and service-package pages. 2–4 plans; mark at most one as featured. Keep inclusions parallel across plans. Avoid: Prices the owner hasn't confirmed; hidden fees; more than ~6 inclusions per plan; using it for a single product (use the product block).

### `product` — Product

Sells one product from the shop: image, price, options and an Add to cart button. Use: Featuring a single product on a landing page or inside a story. ### `quote` — Quote

A short, memorable quotation set apart from body text. Use: To pause the reader between sections, or to open a page with an epigraph. `large` is a centred statement, `bar` sits inside reading text. Avoid: Customer reviews (use testimonial); misattributed or invented quotes; quotes longer than three sentences.

Several short quotes from clients or reviews in a swipeable carousel. Avoid: Invented or edited quotes; fewer than three quotes (use testimonial); quotes over three sentences.

- Variants: `slides`, `cards`, `minimal`
- Fields: `label: text ≤ 80`, `quotes: list of { quote: text ≤ 400, name: text ≤ 80, role?: text ≤ 100, photo?: image { src, alt } }`

### `restaurant-menu` — Menu

A restaurant, café or bar menu: sections of dishes with descriptions and prices. Use: Menu pages and hospitality sites. Keep descriptions to one line; mark dietary information accurately. `columns` sets sections side by side on wide screens. Avoid: Out-of-date prices; dietary claims the kitchen can't guarantee; using it for services (use the pricing table).

- Variants: `classic`, `columns`, `minimal`
- Fields: `sections: list of { title: text ≤ 60, note?: text ≤ 160, items: list of { name: text ≤ 80, description?: text ≤ 240, price?: text ≤ 24, dietary: list of { tag: "v" | "vg" | "gf" | "df" | "n" | "spicy" } } }`, `currency?: text ≤ 4`, `legend: boolean`, `footnote?: text ≤ 240`

### `search` — Search

Opens the site's built-in search (Pagefind), which indexes every published page. Use: Sites with a blog, events or many pages — on a resources page, a 404 page or at the top of the journal. `icon` fits tight spaces. Avoid: Small sites of a few pages, where navigation is enough.

- Variants: `field`, `button`, `icon`
- Fields: `placeholder: text ≤ 60`, `shortcutHint: boolean`

### `shape` — Shape

Decorative shapes (blob, arch, sparkle, squiggle…) in palette colors. Use: In grid sections, layered behind or beside images and text to add warmth and brand character. Keep to one or two per section. Avoid: Using shapes to carry meaning or text; bright shapes behind body text that hurt contrast.

- Variants: `solid`, `outline`, `soft`
- Fields: `shape: "circle" | "ring" | "blob" | "arch" | "half-circle" | "pill" | "squircle" | "triangle" | "sparkle" | "star" | "flower" | "wave"`, `color: color`, `size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "fill"`, `rotate: number`, `stretch: boolean`

### `share-buttons` — Share buttons

Share links for the page being viewed (blog posts, events, announcements). Use: At the end of articles and event pages. Avoid: Putting share buttons on every page; more than four or five networks.

- Variants: `icons`, `labels`, `pills`
- Fields: `label?: text ≤ 40`, `networks: list of { network: "x" | "facebook" | "linkedin" | "bluesky" | "threads" | "pinterest" | "email" }`

### `social-feed` — Social feed

A grid of recent posts from the owner's social profile, linking to each post. Use: Near the footer or on about pages to show everyday life. Posts are fetched at publish time with the owner's permission, so no third-party scripts load. Avoid: Embedding other people's posts; feeds as the main content of a page.

- Variants: `grid`, `row`, `mosaic`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `network: "instagram" | "bluesky" | "mastodon" | "pinterest" | "tiktok" | "youtube"`, `handle: text ≤ 80`, `count: "3" | "4" | "6" | "8"`, `followLabel: text ≤ 40`, `posts: list of { image: image { src, alt }, url: link, caption?: text ≤ 200 }`

### `social-links` — Social links

Links to the owner's social media and email. Use: Footers, contact and about pages. Prefer `source: site` so profiles stay in sync across the site. Avoid: Linking to inactive accounts; more than ~6 networks.

- Variants: `icons`, `labels`, `pills`
- Fields: `source: "site" | "custom"`, `profiles: list of { network: "instagram" | "facebook" | "x" | "threads" | "bluesky" | "mastodon" | "linkedin" | "youtube" | "tiktok" | "pinterest" | "github" | "spotify" | "soundcloud" | "bandcamp" | "vimeo" | "behance" | "dribbble" | "substack" | "patreon" | "yelp" | "tripadvisor" | "email" | "website", url: text ≤ 300 }`, `label?: text ≤ 60`

### `spacer` — Spacer

Extra vertical space between blocks, sized from the site's spacing scale. Use: Sparingly, to give a heading or image more air than the default block gap. Avoid: Stacking spacers; using spacers to fake section padding (adjust the section instead).

- Variants: —
- Fields: `height: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl"`, `mobileHeight?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl"`

### `stats` — Stats

Key figures that make a claim concrete (members, years, ratings, outcomes). Use: On about, services and fundraising pages; 3–4 numbers read best. `large` gives each number its own row. Avoid: Invented, rounded-up or unverifiable figures; more than six stats; vanity numbers.

- Variants: `row`, `cards`, `large`
- Fields: `items: list of { value: text ≤ 16, label: text ≤ 80, detail?: text ≤ 140 }`

### `summary` — Summary

Lists items from a collection (blog posts, events, projects, episodes, products) as cards. Use: On the home page and landing pages to surface fresh content: the latest 3 posts, featured projects, upcoming events. `wall` is a masonry of images for portfolios; `carousel` saves space. Avoid: Using it as the main collection page (the collection's own list page does that); mixing unrelated filters; more than ~12 items.

- Variants: `grid`, `list`, `carousel`, `wall`
- Fields: `heading?: text ≤ 80`, `headingLevel: "h2" | "h3" | "h4"`, `source: reference`, `columns: "2" | "3" | "4"`, `showImage: boolean`, `imageAspect?: "1:1" | "4:5" | "2:3" | "3:2" | "16:9" | "21:9"`, `showDate: boolean`, `showExcerpt: boolean`, `showMeta: boolean`, `linkLabel?: text ≤ 30`, `link?: link`, `emptyMessage: text ≤ 160`

### `table` — Comparison table

Compares plans, packages, products or options feature by feature in a real, accessible table. Use: Under a pricing section (full plan comparison), for specs, or 'us vs. the usual way'. 2–4 columns and 4–12 rows read best; use 'yes'/'no' for checks and dashes, group rows to break long lists. Avoid: Layout tables; more than five columns (phones scroll sideways); claims about competitors the owner can't back up; comparisons with named rival brands.

- Variants: `lines`, `striped`, `boxed`
- Fields: `caption?: text ≤ 120`, `corner?: text ≤ 40`, `columns: list of { label: text ≤ 40, detail?: text ≤ 40, highlight: boolean }`, `rows: list of { label: text ≤ 80, group: boolean, cells: list of { value: text ≤ 60 } }`, `note?: text ≤ 200`

### `tabs` — Tabs

Parallel pieces of content shown one at a time, switched by tabs. Use: Comparable options (class styles, service tiers, menus by meal) where visitors want one at a time. 2–5 tabs with short labels. Avoid: Content everyone needs to read (tabs hide it); long labels; sequences (use a timeline) or FAQs (use an accordion).

- Variants: `underline`, `pills`, `vertical`
- Fields: `label: text ≤ 80`, `items: list of { label: text ≤ 40, content: richText }`

### `team` — Team

Introduces the people behind the business: staff, teachers, partners, a board. Use: About and team pages, and near services where visitors choose a person. `circles` suits large teams; `list` gives each bio more room. Avoid: People who haven't agreed to appear; stock photos presented as staff; bios over ~60 words.

- Variants: `grid`, `list`, `circles`
- Fields: `people: list of { name: text ≤ 80, role?: text ≤ 80, photo?: image { src, alt }, bio?: text ≤ 320, link?: link }`, `columns: "2" | "3" | "4"`

### `testimonial` — Testimonial

A short quote from a client or customer, attributed to a named person. Use: Social proof near a call to action or on a services page. Use three side by side (`card`) or one `large` testimonial as a section's centrepiece. Avoid: Inventing testimonials or ratings. Ask the owner for real quotes and permission to use names and photos.

- Variants: `card`, `large`, `minimal`
- Fields: `quote: richText`, `name: text ≤ 80`, `role?: text ≤ 100`, `photo?: image { src, alt }`, `rating?: number`

### `text` — Text

Running text: headings, paragraphs, lists and pull quotes. Use: Any time words carry the section — introductions, stories, policies. Use `columns` for long reading text, `drop-cap` for editorial openings, `callout` for a note that must stand out. Avoid: Walls of text; more than one H1 per page; using bold paragraphs as fake headings. Use the button block for calls to action.

- Variants: `default`, `columns`, `drop-cap`, `callout`
- Fields: `content: richText`

### `timeline` — Timeline

A sequence of dated or numbered milestones. Use: Company or project history, a programme's weeks, a process from enquiry to delivery. `horizontal` suits 3–5 short steps. Avoid: Undated lists (use a list or columns); invented history; more than ~10 milestones.

- Variants: `vertical`, `alternating`, `horizontal`
- Fields: `items: list of { date: text ≤ 40, title: text ≤ 100, text?: text ≤ 400 }`

### `video` — Video

A video from YouTube, Vimeo or PeerTube, or an uploaded video file. Use: Walkthroughs, talks, trailers and atmosphere. The player loads only when a visitor presses play, so pages stay fast. Avoid: Autoplaying sound; background loops longer than ~20 seconds; using a video where a photo says the same thing.

- Variants: `default`, `framed`, `cinematic`
- Fields: `source: "embed" | "file"`, `url?: text ≤ 500`, `file?: media`, `title: text ≤ 120`, `poster?: image { src, alt }`, `caption?: text ≤ 200`, `aspect: "16:9" | "21:9" | "4:3" | "1:1" | "9:16"`, `background: boolean`
